first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence supports signup/onboarding simplification as a durable self-serve growth lever. This is more sustainable than promotional pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention. Verify the two most directly relevant records before committing, while monitoring downstream qualified revenue and lead quality.

mid.rationale: Run a guarded standard experiment combining reduced signup friction with a shorter onboarding flow, focused on self-serve SMB accounts. The evidence directly addresses both current declines: signup simplification lifted activation and qualified revenue, while shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and retention. Monitor qualified revenue and 30-day retention closely because signup simplification showed a small retention decline and has not been replicated beyond SMB; do not broadly roll out yet.

final2.rationale: Run a narrowly targeted, time-limited offer for price-sensitive SMB accounts facing imminent churn, with strict retention and qualified-revenue gates. Prior evidence shows acquisition and revenue lift but materially worse 30-day retention, so this should be an emergency containment test—not a broad pricing response or general growth strategy.
